title: Last-point ordinal indexing adjunction
statement:
Use small ordinary nerves, quasicategories and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a containing universe. Let $\Delta_+$ have objects the finite ordinals $J$, including $\varnothing$, and all monotone maps, and let $\Delta\subset\Delta_+$ contain the nonempty ordinals. Define $D$ to have the same objects as $\Delta_+$ and morphisms $J\to K$ all monotone maps $J\sqcup\{\infty\}\to K\sqcup\{\infty\}$ fixing the new greatest element, composed as maps. Let $i:\Delta\to D$ and $j:\Delta_+\to D$ extend monotone maps to fix the new last element, with no ordinary element sent to it. Let $U:D\to\Delta$ send $J$ to $J\sqcup\{\infty\}$ and each arrow to its underlying monotone map. Then $i\dashv U$, with the natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(iA,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(A,UJ)$$
given by restriction to $A$, and $\varnothing$ is initial in $D$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16 (printed p.553), definition of the category of last-point-preserving ordinal maps, and Lemma 6.1.3.17: explicit ordinary indexing adjunction supporting the right shift. No Stacks tag states this indexing assertion.

proof.text: Write $J^+=J\sqcup\{\infty_J\}$, ordered with every element of $J$ below $\infty_J$. Identity maps and composites of monotone maps fixing the distinguished last element again fix it; their category laws are the laws of function composition. For a monotone $h:J\to K$, its extension $h^+$ sends $x\in J$ to $h(x)\in K$ and sends $\infty_J$ to $\infty_K$. It is monotone: the only additional inequalities to check have upper endpoint $\infty_J$, and their images are below $\infty_K$. Extensions preserve identities and composition pointwise, proving that $j$ and its restriction $i$ are functors. Each $J^+$ is nonempty, and forgetting the distinguished-point condition preserves identities and composition, so $U$ is a functor to $\Delta$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.16, printed p.553: definition of the ordinal category; Lemma 6.1.3.17, printed p.554: adjoining the last element. Agent verification of the category and functor laws.

proof.text: For $A\in\Delta$ and $J\in D$, restrict $f:A^+\to J^+$ to $A$ to obtain $\Phi_{A,J}(f):A\to J^+$. Conversely, for any monotone $g:A\to J^+$ define $\widehat g:A^+\to J^+$ by $\widehat g|_A=g$ and $\widehat g(\infty_A)=\infty_J$. The extension is monotone, since $g(a)\leq\infty_J$ for every $a\in A$, and it fixes the last element. Restricting $\widehat g$ gives $g$; extending the restriction of $f$ gives $f$, including at $\infty_A$ since $f$ fixes it. Thus $\Phi_{A,J}$ is the asserted bijection. The values of $g$ are allowed to equal $\infty_J$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.16, printed p.553, last-point-preserving maps: agent restriction-and-extension calculation.

proof.text: For a monotone $a:A\prime\to A$ in $\Delta$ and an arrow $b:J\to K$ in $D$, and for $f:iA\to J$, restriction gives the equality $\Phi_{A\prime,K}(b\circ f\circ i(a))=U(b)\circ\Phi_{A,J}(f)\circ a$: evaluation at $x\in A\prime$ gives $b(f(a(x)))$ on both sides. This also holds when $b$ sends an ordinary element to $\infty_K$. Taking either $a$ or $b$ to be an identity proves naturality separately in both variables. Hence these are natural Hom-set bijections for $i\dashv U$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.16, printed p.553, same explicit ordinal maps: agent verification of both naturality variables.

proof.text: The unit is $\eta_A:A\to UiA=A^+$, $a\mapsto a$. The counit $\varepsilon_J:iUJ\to J$ has underlying map $(J^+)^+\to J^+$ that fixes every element of the original $J^+$ and sends the newly added outer last element to $\infty_J$. It is monotone and last-point-preserving. The unit is natural because extensions agree with the original maps on original elements; the counit is natural because for $b:J\to K$, $b\circ\varepsilon_J=\varepsilon_K\circ iU(b)$, both sides being $b(x)$ on $x\in J^+$ and $\infty_K$ on the outer last element. The composite $\varepsilon_{iA}\circ i(\eta_A)$ fixes $a\in A$ and the added last element, hence is $1_{iA}$. The composite $U(\varepsilon_J)\circ\eta_{UJ}$ fixes every $x\in J^+$, hence is $1_{UJ}$. These give the adjunction explicitly with both triangle identities; its Hom bijection sends $f$ to $U(f)\circ\eta_A$, exactly restriction.

source.place: Lemmas 6.1.3.16–17, printed pp.553–554, same ordinal category and shift: agent unit, counit and triangle calculation.

proof.text: A morphism $\varnothing\to J$ in $D$ is a monotone map $\{\infty_\varnothing\}\to J^+$ fixing the distinguished last element. Its only possible value is $\infty_J$, and this map is monotone. Thus there is exactly one such arrow for every $J$, including $J=\varnothing$, which is precisely initiality in the ordinary category $D$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.16, printed p.553, definition of the ordinal category: agent singleton calculation.

proof_origin.place: Explicit finite-ordinal calculation from the definition in HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16, printed p.553, and shift in Lemma 6.1.3.17, printed p.554. The adjunction and triangle identities are expanded here, not quoted as a theorem of HTT; an archived literature copy is WANTED in report.md.
